source: CIS Controls v7.1 + cyber.trackr.live/api CCI lookup

mappings.cis_title: Explicitly Not Mapped
mappings.coverage_assessment: CIS explicitly does not map this control to any CIS Controls safeguard.

mappings.cis_title: Utilize an Active Discovery Tool

primary_cci.reasoning: SI-4.2 — monitors the system to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks. Active discovery tools are a form of system monitoring that detects unauthorized assets/connections.

mappings.coverage_assessment: SI-4 broadly covers system monitoring including active network discovery. Direct match for active scanning/discovery tools.

mappings.cis_title: Use a Passive Asset Discovery Tool

primary_cci.reasoning: SI-4.2 — system monitoring to detect attacks and indicators. Passive discovery is a monitoring technique that observes network traffic rather than actively probing.

supporting_ccis.reasoning: CM-8.1 — develop/document inventory that accurately reflects the system. Passive discovery feeds asset inventory.

mappings.coverage_assessment: SI-4 covers passive monitoring techniques. CM-8 adds inventory context since passive discovery is used to maintain asset awareness.

mappings.cis_title: Use DHCP Logging to Update Asset Inventory

primary_cci.reasoning: CM-8.1 — develop/document inventory that accurately reflects the current system. DHCP logging is a mechanism to keep hardware asset inventory accurate and current.

mappings.coverage_assessment: CM-8 covers maintaining accurate system component inventory. DHCP logging is a technique to ensure inventory reflects actual network-connected devices.

mappings.cis_title: Maintain Detailed Asset Inventory

primary_cci.reasoning: CM-8.1 requires developing an inventory of information system components that accurately reflects the current system.

supporting_ccis.reasoning: CM-8.3 requires inventory at the level of granularity deemed necessary for tracking and reporting.
CM-8.7 requires reviewing and updating the inventory per organization-defined frequency.

mappings.coverage_assessment: Strong coverage. CM-8 is the definitive NIST control for system component inventory.

mappings.cis_title: Maintain Asset Inventory Information

primary_cci.reasoning: CM-8.1 — develop/document inventory that accurately reflects the current system. Direct match: maintaining asset inventory information is the core requirement of CM-8.

supporting_ccis.reasoning: CM-8.7 — reviews and updates the component inventory per defined frequency. Covers the ongoing maintenance aspect.

mappings.coverage_assessment: CM-8 is the canonical NIST control for asset inventory management. Near-perfect alignment.

mappings.cis_title: Address Unauthorized Assets

primary_cci.reasoning: CM-8.1 — inventory that accurately reflects the system. Addressing unauthorized assets requires knowing what is authorized vs. not, which is the inventory's purpose.

supporting_ccis.reasoning: SI-4.2 — monitoring to detect attacks and unauthorized connections. Detecting unauthorized assets is a monitoring function.

mappings.coverage_assessment: CM-8 combined with CM-8(3) (automated unauthorized component detection) covers this best. Primary CCI from CM-8 base control since CM-8(3) CCIs tie to inventory accuracy.

mappings.cis_title: Deploy Port Level Access Control

primary_cci.reasoning: SC-7.1 — monitors and controls communications at the external boundary and key internal boundaries. Port-level access control (802.1X, NAC) is boundary protection at the network port level.

mappings.coverage_assessment: SC-7 covers boundary protection including port-level access controls. 802.1X and NAC are implementations of boundary protection at the physical/data-link layer.

mappings.cis_title: Utilize Client Certificates to Authenticate Hardware Assets

primary_cci.reasoning: IA-3.2 — uniquely identifies organization-defined devices before establishing connections. Client certificates are a device identification and authentication mechanism.

supporting_ccis.reasoning: IA-3.3 — authenticates organization-defined devices before establishing connections. The authentication complement to identification.

mappings.coverage_assessment: IA-3 is the exact NIST control for device identification and authentication. Client certificates are a primary mechanism for implementing IA-3.

mappings.cis_title: Maintain Inventory of Authorized Software

primary_cci.reasoning: CM-8.1 — develop/document inventory that accurately reflects the current system. CM-8 covers both hardware and software component inventory.

mappings.coverage_assessment: CM-8 covers system component inventory including software. The control statements explicitly reference software components in the discussion.

mappings.cis_title: Ensure Software is Supported by Vendor

primary_cci.reasoning: SA-22.1 — component replacement verification. SA-22 directly addresses replacing system components when vendor support is no longer available.

mappings.coverage_assessment: SA-22 (Unsupported System Components) is the exact NIST control for ensuring software/firmware has active vendor support. Direct alignment.

mappings.cis_title: Utilize Software Inventory Tools

primary_cci.reasoning: CM-8.1 — develop/document inventory that accurately reflects the system. Software inventory tools are the mechanism to implement the CM-8 inventory requirement.

mappings.coverage_assessment: CM-8 covers system component inventory. The use of automated tools is addressed in CM-8(2) (automated maintenance) but the base control CCI captures the requirement.

mappings.cis_title: Track Software Inventory Information

primary_cci.reasoning: CM-8.5 — inventory that includes organization-defined information for effective component accountability. Tracking specific software inventory attributes (name, version, vendor, etc.) maps to accountability information.

mappings.coverage_assessment: CM-8 assessment procedure 5 specifically covers including organization-defined accountability information in the inventory, which is what tracking software attributes achieves.

mappings.cis_title: Integrate Software and Hardware Asset Inventories

primary_cci.reasoning: CM-8.2 — inventory includes all components within the authorization boundary. An integrated inventory that covers both hardware and software ensures completeness within the boundary.

supporting_ccis.reasoning: CM-8.1 — inventory that accurately reflects the current system. Integration of HW/SW inventories improves accuracy.

mappings.coverage_assessment: CM-8 covers comprehensive system component inventory. Integrating hardware and software inventories ensures completeness per CM-8a.2.

mappings.cis_title: Address Unapproved Software

primary_cci.reasoning: CM-7.1 — system configured for essential capabilities only. Addressing unapproved software is about restricting system functionality to only authorized/approved software.

mappings.coverage_assessment: CM-7 (Least Functionality) covers restricting software to only approved/needed components. Directly addresses removing or preventing unapproved software.

mappings.cis_title: Utilize Application Whitelisting

primary_cci.reasoning: CM-7(5).3 — employs deny-all, permit-by-exception policy for software execution. This is the literal definition of application whitelisting.

supporting_ccis.reasoning: CM-7(5).2 — identifies authorized software programs. The identification step that precedes whitelisting enforcement.

mappings.coverage_assessment: CM-7(5) is titled 'Authorized Software / Whitelisting' — exact match. The deny-all, permit-by-exception policy is application whitelisting by definition.

mappings.cis_title: Implement Application Whitelisting of Libraries

primary_cci.reasoning: CM-7(5).3 — deny-all, permit-by-exception for authorized software. Libraries are a subset of software programs; the whitelisting principle extends to libraries and DLLs.

mappings.coverage_assessment: CM-7(5) covers whitelisting of software programs, which includes libraries. The control scope encompasses all executable code including shared libraries.

mappings.cis_title: Implement Application Whitelisting of Scripts

primary_cci.reasoning: CM-7(5).3 — deny-all, permit-by-exception for authorized software. Scripts are a form of software program covered by the whitelisting policy.

mappings.coverage_assessment: CM-7(5) covers whitelisting of software programs, which includes scripts. The deny-all policy applies to all executable content including interpreted scripts.

mappings.cis_title: Physically or Logically Segregate High Risk Applications

primary_cci.reasoning: SC-7.2 — implements subnetworks for publicly accessible components that are physically/logically separated from internal networks. Segregation of high-risk applications is boundary protection through isolation.

mappings.coverage_assessment: SC-7 covers boundary protection including physical and logical separation of system components. Segregating high-risk applications aligns with subnetwork isolation requirements.

mappings.cis_title: Run Automated Vulnerability Scanning Tools

primary_cci.reasoning: RA-5.1 — defines scan frequency for vulnerability monitoring. Running automated vulnerability scanning is the core requirement of RA-5.

supporting_ccis.reasoning: RA-5.6 — employs interoperable vulnerability scanning tools. Addresses the 'automated tools' aspect specifically.

mappings.coverage_assessment: RA-5 (Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning) is the exact NIST control for automated vulnerability scanning. Direct alignment.

mappings.cis_title: Perform Authenticated Vulnerability Scanning

primary_cci.reasoning: RA-5.1 — defines vulnerability scan frequency and approach. Authenticated scanning is a more thorough form of vulnerability scanning covered by RA-5.

mappings.coverage_assessment: RA-5 covers all forms of vulnerability scanning. Authenticated scanning provides deeper system analysis and is an implementation detail of the scanning requirement.

mappings.cis_title: Protect Dedicated Assessment Accounts

primary_cci.reasoning: AC-6.1 requires employing least privilege, allowing only authorized accesses necessary for assigned tasks.

supporting_ccis.reasoning: AC-6(5).2 restricts privileged accounts to organization-defined personnel or roles.

mappings.coverage_assessment: Good coverage. AC-6 (least privilege) fits protecting dedicated assessment accounts.

mappings.cis_title: Deploy Automated Operating System Patch Management Tools

primary_cci.reasoning: SI-2.1 — identify, report, and correct system flaws. Automated OS patch management is the primary mechanism for flaw remediation.

supporting_ccis.reasoning: SI-2.9 — installs software updates within organization-defined timeframes. The automated deployment aspect of patch management.

mappings.coverage_assessment: SI-2 (Flaw Remediation) is the exact NIST control for patch management. Automated tools are the mechanism to implement timely flaw correction.

mappings.cis_title: Deploy Automated Software Patch Management Tools

primary_cci.reasoning: SI-2.1 — identify, report, and correct system flaws. Software patch management (beyond OS) is also flaw remediation.

mappings.coverage_assessment: SI-2 covers all flaw remediation including application-level software patching. Same control family as OS patching.

mappings.cis_title: Compare Back-to-Back Vulnerability Scans

primary_cci.reasoning: RA-5.7 — analyzes vulnerability scan reports/results. Comparing back-to-back scans is an analysis technique to identify remediation progress and new vulnerabilities.

mappings.coverage_assessment: RA-5 covers vulnerability scan analysis. Comparing successive scans is part of the analysis and remediation verification process.

mappings.cis_title: Utilize a Risk-Rating Process

primary_cci.reasoning: RA-3.1 — assesses risk including likelihood and magnitude of harm from unauthorized access. A risk-rating process is the implementation of risk assessment.

mappings.coverage_assessment: RA-3 (Risk Assessment) is the exact NIST control for risk rating/assessment processes. Direct alignment.

mappings.cis_title: Maintain Inventory of Administrative Accounts

primary_cci.reasoning: AC-2.1 requires defining information system account types that support organizational missions.

supporting_ccis.reasoning: AC-2.9 requires specifying access authorizations (privileges) for each account.
AC-2.22 requires reviewing accounts for compliance with account management requirements.

mappings.coverage_assessment: Strong coverage. AC-2 (Account Management) is the definitive control for managing and inventorying system accounts.

mappings.cis_title: Change Default Passwords

primary_cci.reasoning: IA-5.12 explicitly requires changing default content of authenticators prior to information system installation.

mappings.coverage_assessment: Excellent coverage. CCI-001989 (IA-5.12) is a direct, precise match for changing default passwords.

mappings.cis_title: Ensure the Use of Dedicated Administrative Accounts

primary_cci.reasoning: AC-6(5).2 requires restricting privileged accounts to organization-defined personnel or roles.

supporting_ccis.reasoning: AC-6.1 enforces least privilege for administrative tasks.

mappings.coverage_assessment: Strong coverage. AC-6(5) specifically addresses privileged accounts and restricting them to defined personnel/roles.

mappings.cis_title: Use Unique Passwords

primary_cci.reasoning: IA-5(1).1 enforces password complexity requirements for password-based authentication.

supporting_ccis.reasoning: IA-5(1).18 prohibits password reuse for a defined number of generations.
IA-5.3 ensures authenticators have sufficient strength of mechanism.

mappings.coverage_assessment: Good coverage. IA-5(1) addresses password-based authentication including complexity and reuse prevention.

mappings.cis_title: Use Multifactor Authentication For All Administrative Access

primary_cci.reasoning: IA-2(1).1 requires MFA for network access to privileged accounts.

mappings.coverage_assessment: Excellent coverage. CCI-000765 (IA-2(1).1) is a direct match for MFA on administrative access.

mappings.cis_title: Use Dedicated Workstations For All Administrative Tasks

primary_cci.reasoning: AC-6(5).2 — restricts privileged accounts to organization-defined personnel or roles. Dedicated admin workstations enforce privileged account restrictions by separating admin functions to specific systems.

supporting_ccis.reasoning: AC-6(5).1 — defines personnel/roles to whom privileged accounts are restricted. Identifying who uses dedicated admin workstations.

mappings.coverage_assessment: AC-6(5) (Privileged Accounts) covers restricting privileged access to defined roles/systems. Dedicated admin workstations enforce this by physically/logically separating privileged operations.

mappings.cis_title: Limit Access to Script Tools

primary_cci.reasoning: CM-7.1 — system configured to provide only essential capabilities. Limiting access to script tools restricts system functionality to reduce attack surface.

supporting_ccis.reasoning: CM-7.3 — enforces restrictions on defined functions, ports, protocols, software. Script tools are software that can be restricted per policy.

mappings.coverage_assessment: CM-7 (Least Functionality) covers restricting unnecessary system capabilities. Limiting script tool access reduces attack surface by removing unneeded functionality.

mappings.cis_title: Log and Alert on Changes to Administrative Group Membership

primary_cci.reasoning: AU-12c requires generating audit records for defined events. Admin group membership changes are auditable events.

supporting_ccis.reasoning: AC-2g requires monitoring account/group usage, supporting alerting on admin group changes.

mappings.coverage_assessment: AU-12c covers audit record generation. AC-2g provides supporting coverage for monitoring account/group usage.

mappings.cis_title: Log and Alert on Unsuccessful Administrative Account Login

primary_cci.reasoning: AC-7.2 directly addresses enforcing limits on consecutive invalid logon attempts, which is the mechanism underlying logging and alerting on unsuccessful admin logins

supporting_ccis.reasoning: AU-2.1 requires the system to be capable of auditing defined events, including failed logon attempts

mappings.coverage_assessment: AC-7 covers the enforcement side (detecting/responding to failed logons); AU-2 covers the audit requirement. AC-7 is primary because the safeguard focuses on admin account login failures.

mappings.cis_title: Establish Secure Configurations

primary_cci.reasoning: CM-6b requires implementing security configuration settings.

supporting_ccis.reasoning: CM-6a requires establishing configuration settings.
CM-6a requires documenting configuration settings.

mappings.coverage_assessment: CM-6b is a direct match for establishing secure configurations.

mappings.cis_title: Maintain Secure Images

primary_cci.reasoning: CM-2.1 requires developing and documenting a current baseline configuration, which directly maps to maintaining secure (golden) images

supporting_ccis.reasoning: CM-2.2 requires maintaining the baseline under configuration control, ensuring images remain current and secure

mappings.coverage_assessment: CM-2 baseline configuration directly covers maintaining secure/golden images as the authoritative system configuration reference.

mappings.cis_title: Securely Store Master Images

primary_cci.reasoning: CM-2.2 requires maintaining the baseline configuration under configuration control, which encompasses secure storage of master images

mappings.coverage_assessment: CM-2 covers maintaining baselines under configuration control. Secure storage of master images is an inherent part of maintaining configuration control over baselines.

mappings.cis_title: Deploy System Configuration Management Tools

primary_cci.reasoning: CM-6.2 requires establishing configuration settings using defined security checklists, which directly maps to deploying configuration management tooling

supporting_ccis.reasoning: CM-6.5 requires implementing the security configuration settings, covering the deployment/enforcement aspect

mappings.coverage_assessment: CM-6 configuration settings covers deploying tools that establish and enforce system configuration. Preferred over CM-3 (change control) because this safeguard is about configuration management tooling, not change approval processes.

mappings.cis_title: Implement Automated Configuration Monitoring Systems

primary_cci.reasoning: SI-7.2 requires employing integrity verification tools to detect unauthorized changes to software/firmware/information, directly mapping to automated configuration monitoring

supporting_ccis.reasoning: CM-6.11 requires monitoring configuration setting changes per policies, covering the configuration-specific monitoring aspect

mappings.coverage_assessment: SI-7 integrity verification tools detect unauthorized changes, which is the core function of automated configuration monitoring. CM-6 monitoring provides supporting coverage for configuration settings specifically.

mappings.cis_title: Utilize Three Synchronized Time Sources

primary_cci.reasoning: AU-8.1 requires the system to use internal clocks for generating audit record timestamps, which depends on synchronized time sources

supporting_ccis.reasoning: AU-8.4 requires timestamps mappable to UTC/GMT, which necessitates synchronized authoritative time sources

mappings.coverage_assessment: AU-8 time stamps directly covers time synchronization requirements. The need for multiple synchronized sources ensures reliable, accurate timestamps for audit records.

mappings.cis_title: Activate audit logging

primary_cci.reasoning: AU-12a requires providing audit record generation capability for auditable events.

supporting_ccis.reasoning: AU-2d defines which events are to be audited.

mappings.coverage_assessment: AU-12a is the most precise match for activating audit logging capability.

mappings.cis_title: Enable Detailed Logging

primary_cci.reasoning: AU-3.1 requires audit records to contain information establishing what type of event occurred, which is the foundational requirement for detailed logging

supporting_ccis.reasoning: AU-3.5 requires audit records to establish the outcome of the event, a key component of detailed logging

mappings.coverage_assessment: AU-3 content of audit records directly addresses what detail must be captured in logs (event type, time, location, source, outcome, identity).

mappings.cis_title: Ensure Adequate Storage for Logs

primary_cci.reasoning: AU-4.2 requires allocating audit record storage capacity per defined requirements, directly mapping to ensuring adequate log storage

mappings.coverage_assessment: AU-4 audit log storage capacity is a direct match. AU-4.2 specifically addresses allocating sufficient storage for audit records.

mappings.cis_title: Central Log Management

primary_cci.reasoning: AU-6.1 requires reviewing and analyzing audit records for indications of inappropriate or unusual activity, which necessitates centralized log management for effective analysis

supporting_ccis.reasoning: SI-4.2 requires monitoring the system to detect attacks, supporting centralized monitoring capabilities

mappings.coverage_assessment: AU-6 audit record review/analysis/reporting is the primary driver for centralized log management. Central collection enables the review and correlation activities AU-6 requires.

mappings.cis_title: Deploy SIEM or Log Analytic Tools

primary_cci.reasoning: SI-4.2 requires monitoring the system to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks, which is the core function of SIEM and log analytics tools

supporting_ccis.reasoning: SI-4.8 requires deploying monitoring devices strategically to collect essential information, covering SIEM sensor/collector deployment

mappings.coverage_assessment: SI-4 system monitoring directly covers SIEM deployment. SIEM tools are the primary technical implementation of the monitoring capabilities SI-4 requires.

mappings.cis_title: Regularly Review Logs

primary_cci.reasoning: AU-6a requires reviewing and analyzing audit records on a defined frequency.

supporting_ccis.reasoning: AU-6b requires reporting findings from log review.

mappings.coverage_assessment: AU-6a is a direct match for regular log review and analysis.

mappings.cis_title: Regularly Tune SIEM

primary_cci.reasoning: SI-4.1 requires defining monitoring objectives for attacks and potential indicators, and tuning SIEM is the operational activity of refining those monitoring objectives and detection rules

supporting_ccis.reasoning: SI-4.13 requires increasing monitoring when risk indicators suggest elevated threats, which is an aspect of SIEM tuning

mappings.coverage_assessment: SI-4 monitoring objectives and device tuning. Regularly tuning SIEM aligns with defining/refining monitoring objectives (SI-4.1) and adjusting monitoring based on risk (SI-4.13).

mappings.cis_title: Ensure Use of Only Fully Supported Browsers and Email Clients

primary_cci.reasoning: SA-22.1 requires replacing system components when support is no longer available from the developer/vendor, directly addressing the use of only supported software

mappings.coverage_assessment: SA-22 unsupported system components is a direct match. It requires replacing components that have lost vendor support, which is exactly what this safeguard mandates for browsers and email clients.

mappings.cis_title: Disable Unnecessary or Unauthorized Browser or Email Client Plugins

primary_cci.reasoning: CM-7.1 requires configuring the system to provide only essential capabilities, directly mapping to disabling unnecessary browser/email plugins

supporting_ccis.reasoning: CM-7.3 requires prohibiting or restricting use of defined functions/ports/protocols/services, covering the enforcement of plugin restrictions

mappings.coverage_assessment: CM-7 least functionality is a direct match. Disabling unnecessary plugins is a specific instance of configuring systems to provide only essential capabilities.

mappings.cis_title: Limit Use of Scripting Languages in Web Browsers and Email Clients

primary_cci.reasoning: CM-7.1 requires configuring the system to provide only essential capabilities; limiting scripting languages is restricting functionality to essential needs

supporting_ccis.reasoning: CM-7.3 requires prohibiting or restricting defined functions, covering the specific restriction of scripting language execution

mappings.coverage_assessment: CM-7 least functionality covers restricting scripting languages as part of limiting system capabilities to only what is essential for operations.

mappings.cis_title: Maintain and Enforce Network-Based URL Filters

primary_cci.reasoning: SC-7.1 requires monitoring and controlling communications at external boundaries; URL filtering is a boundary protection mechanism that controls outbound web traffic

supporting_ccis.reasoning: AC-4.1 enforces approved authorizations for information flow within the system, supporting URL-based flow control

mappings.coverage_assessment: SC-7 boundary protection covers URL filtering as a mechanism for monitoring and controlling communications at system boundaries. AC-4 information flow enforcement provides supporting coverage.

mappings.cis_title: Subscribe to URL-Categorization Service

primary_cci.reasoning: SC-7.1 monitoring and controlling communications at boundaries requires URL categorization services to effectively classify and filter web traffic

mappings.coverage_assessment: SC-7 boundary protection. URL categorization services enable effective boundary controls by classifying web destinations for filtering decisions.

mappings.cis_title: Log All URL Requests

primary_cci.reasoning: AU-12.1 requires providing audit record generation capability for defined auditable events; logging URL requests is generating audit records for web access events

supporting_ccis.reasoning: AU-12.5 requires generating audit records for defined events with defined content, covering the actual generation of URL request logs

mappings.coverage_assessment: AU-12 audit record generation covers logging URL requests as a specific type of auditable event. AU-12 is preferred over SI-4 because this safeguard is about generating log records, not monitoring/alerting.

mappings.cis_title: Use of DNS Filtering Services

primary_cci.reasoning: SC-7.1 monitoring and controlling communications at boundaries; DNS filtering is a boundary protection mechanism that controls network communications at the DNS resolution layer

supporting_ccis.reasoning: SC-20.1 provides data origin authentication for name resolution, supporting DNS integrity aspects of filtering

mappings.coverage_assessment: SC-7 boundary protection is primary for DNS filtering as a boundary control mechanism. SC-20 provides supporting coverage for DNS integrity/authentication aspects.

mappings.cis_title: Implement DMARC and Enable Receiver-Side Verification

primary_cci.reasoning: SI-8.1 requires employing spam protection mechanisms at entry points to detect and act on unsolicited messages; DMARC is a key email authentication mechanism that prevents spoofed/spam email

mappings.coverage_assessment: SI-8 spam protection covers DMARC as an email authentication and spam prevention mechanism at system entry points. DMARC validates sender authenticity, which is a core spam protection function.

mappings.cis_title: Block Unnecessary File Types

primary_cci.reasoning: CM-7.1 configuring the system to provide only essential capabilities; blocking unnecessary file types restricts system functionality to only needed file formats

supporting_ccis.reasoning: SI-3.1 employing malicious code protection at entry points covers blocking dangerous file types as a malware prevention measure

mappings.coverage_assessment: CM-7 least functionality is primary for blocking file types as a restriction of unnecessary capabilities. SI-3 provides supporting coverage when the blocked file types are associated with malware vectors.

mappings.cis_title: Sandbox All Email Attachments

primary_cci.reasoning: SI-3.1 requires employing malicious code protection mechanisms at entry points to detect malicious code; sandboxing email attachments is a malicious code detection technique at the email entry point

mappings.coverage_assessment: SI-3 malicious code protection at entry points directly covers sandboxing email attachments as a detection/prevention mechanism for malware delivered via email.

mappings.cis_title: Utilize Centrally Managed Anti-Malware Software

primary_cci.reasoning: SI-3.1 requires employing malicious code protection mechanisms at entry points; centrally managed anti-malware is the primary implementation of this requirement

supporting_ccis.reasoning: SI-3.10 requires configuring malicious code protection to perform defined actions in response to detection, covering the central management/response aspect

mappings.coverage_assessment: SI-3 malicious code protection is a direct match for centrally managed anti-malware software deployment and operation.

mappings.cis_title: Ensure Anti-Malware Software and Signatures Are Updated

primary_cci.reasoning: SI-3.5 explicitly requires updating malicious code protection mechanisms whenever new releases are available per configuration management policy

mappings.coverage_assessment: SI-3.5 (CCI-001240) is an exact match -- it specifically addresses updating anti-malware mechanisms and signatures when new releases are available.

mappings.cis_title: Enable Operating System Anti-Exploitation Features

primary_cci.reasoning: SI-16.2 requires implementing defined security safeguards to protect system memory from unauthorized code execution, directly covering OS anti-exploitation features like DEP and ASLR

mappings.coverage_assessment: SI-16 memory protection is a direct match. OS anti-exploitation features (DEP, ASLR, SEHOP) are the specific technical implementations of SI-16 memory protection safeguards.

mappings.cis_title: Configure Anti-Malware Scanning of Removable Devices

primary_cci.reasoning: SI-3.1 requires malicious code protection at entry points; removable media is an entry point for malicious code

supporting_ccis.reasoning: MP-7.4 requires restricting or prohibiting use of defined media types using defined safeguards, covering the removable device control aspect

mappings.coverage_assessment: SI-3 malicious code protection at entry points covers scanning removable devices as a malware entry vector. MP-7 media use provides supporting coverage for the removable device control policies.

mappings.cis_title: Configure Devices to Not Auto-Run Content

primary_cci.reasoning: CM-7.1 - configuring systems to provide only essential capabilities; disabling auto-run removes unnecessary functionality

supporting_ccis.reasoning: CM-7.3 - prohibiting or restricting use of organization-defined functions (auto-run)

mappings.coverage_assessment: CM-7 least functionality directly covers restricting auto-run as unnecessary/risky default behavior

mappings.cis_title: Centralize Anti-Malware Logging

primary_cci.reasoning: AU-6(4).1 - centrally review and analyze audit records from multiple components, directly maps to centralizing anti-malware logs

supporting_ccis.reasoning: AU-6(3).1 - correlate audit records across different repositories for situational awareness

mappings.coverage_assessment: AU-6(4) central review and analysis is the best match for centralizing anti-malware logging across an enterprise

mappings.cis_title: Enable DNS Query Logging

primary_cci.reasoning: AU-12.1 - audit record generation capability for auditable events; DNS queries are auditable events requiring log generation

supporting_ccis.reasoning: AU-12.5 - generates audit records for defined events with defined content

mappings.coverage_assessment: AU-12 audit generation covers enabling logging for DNS queries as an auditable event type

mappings.cis_title: Enable Command-Line Audit Logging

primary_cci.reasoning: AU-12.1 - audit record generation capability; command-line execution is an auditable event requiring logging

supporting_ccis.reasoning: AU-3.1 - audit records containing what type of event occurred, relevant to capturing command-line content

mappings.coverage_assessment: AU-12 audit generation is primary; AU-3 content requirements ensure command-line details are captured in records

mappings.cis_title: Associate Active Ports, Services, and Protocols to Asset Inventory

primary_cci.reasoning: CM-8.1 - develop and document inventory of system components that accurately reflects the current system, including active ports/services/protocols

supporting_ccis.reasoning: CM-8.5 - inventory includes organization-defined information for effective component accountability

mappings.coverage_assessment: CM-8 system component inventory directly covers maintaining inventory of ports, services, and protocols associated with assets

mappings.cis_title: Ensure Only Approved Ports, Protocols and Services Are Running

primary_cci.reasoning: CM-7b requires prohibiting or restricting use of defined functions, ports, protocols, and services.

supporting_ccis.reasoning: CM-7a requires providing only essential capabilities (least functionality).

mappings.coverage_assessment: CM-7b is a direct and precise match for restricting ports/protocols/services.

mappings.cis_title: Perform Regular Automated Port Scans

primary_cci.reasoning: RA-5.1 - scans for vulnerabilities at organization-defined frequency; port scanning is a vulnerability scanning activity

supporting_ccis.reasoning: RA-5.6 - employs scanning tools and techniques that facilitate interoperability and automation

mappings.coverage_assessment: RA-5 vulnerability scanning covers automated port scans as part of regular vulnerability assessment processes

mappings.cis_title: Apply Host-Based Firewalls or Port-Filtering

primary_cci.reasoning: SC-7.1 - monitors and controls communications at external boundary and key internal boundaries; host-based firewalls implement boundary protection

mappings.coverage_assessment: SC-7 boundary protection covers host-based firewalls and port filtering as system boundary controls

mappings.cis_title: Implement Application Firewalls

primary_cci.reasoning: SC-7.1 - monitors and controls communications at external boundary and key internal boundaries; application firewalls operate at application layer boundaries

supporting_ccis.reasoning: SC-7.2 - implements subnetworks for publicly accessible components with logical separation

mappings.coverage_assessment: SC-7 boundary protection covers application firewalls as application-layer boundary enforcement

mappings.cis_title: Ensure Regular Automated Backups

primary_cci.reasoning: CP-9.2 - conducts backups of user-level information at organization-defined frequency consistent with recovery objectives

supporting_ccis.reasoning: CP-9.4 - conducts backups of system-level information at organization-defined frequency

mappings.coverage_assessment: CP-9 system backup directly addresses regular automated backups for both user-level and system-level information

mappings.cis_title: Perform Complete System Backups

primary_cci.reasoning: CP-9.4 - conducts backups of system-level information; complete system backups are system-level backup operations

supporting_ccis.reasoning: CP-9.2 - conducts backups of user-level information, complementing system-level for complete backups
